items.title: TOM'S UPDATED WILDCARD DRAFT! ✅ | FPL GAMEWEEK 6 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Bukayo Saka edges Cole Palmer in Gameweek 6 wildcard draft
items.summary:
The Gameweek 6 wildcard is built around a deep, rotation-friendly 15 rather than premium-heavy structure. Erling Haaland remains non-negotiable despite Manchester City travelling to Liverpool, with Ipswich in Gameweek 7 reinforcing the case to keep him. Bukayo Saka is preferred to Cole Palmer as the premium midfielder and is a viable captain against Leeds in Gameweek 6: he is Arsenal’s leading shooter and big-chance recipient, is still underperforming his expected goals despite three returns, and looks likely to retain strong league minutes around manageable midweek fixtures. Palmer retains explosive potential and penalties, but Chelsea’s threat is more shared between João Pedro’s finishing and Morgan Rogers’ creation.

The defence prioritises Arsenal security and value, with Riccardo Calafiori and Cristhian Mosquera joined by Malick Thiaw, Jan Paul van Hecke and Bournemouth’s António Silva. Calafiori offers both clean-sheet and attacking upside, while Mosquera is considered too cheap to ignore as long as he keeps his place. Thiaw covers Gameweek 6 and Gameweek 8 fixtures, Van Hecke is a DefCon option to monitor after withdrawing from the Netherlands squad, and Silva is a longer-term Bournemouth play rather than a starter at Chelsea this week. Bournemouth’s run from Gameweeks 7-14, including Sunderland, Leeds, Ipswich, Forest, Fulham and Brighton, makes their assets increasingly attractive. Bart Verbruggen and Hull’s Salah provide the preferred pair of rotating £4.5m goalkeepers, although Raya, Petrovic and Kinsky remain alternatives.

Morgan Gibbs-White, Kevin Schade, Morgan Rogers and Pascal Groß complete the midfield. Gibbs-White is the least certain selection but supplies penalties, a differential and an easy route to free funds later, potentially for Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier. Schade stays because Brentford look strong, his minutes are secure and his pace suits transition matches, even against Liverpool. Groß is initially benched but offers reliable minutes, penalties and useful rotation once difficult trips to Liverpool and Manchester City pass.

João Pedro is the major wildcard uncertainty after reports of a knee issue and a specialist consultation. A strong first substitute in Groß makes holding him viable for one absence, but missing multiple gameweeks would make the decision costly; Igor Thiago is a similarly priced alternative, while downgrading Gibbs-White could reopen a route to Isak. Gonzalo García is the chosen Fulham attacker for a favourable run beginning with Ipswich, Hull and Coventry, despite being a differential punt with limited output so far. If García fails to deliver, Calvert-Lewin is an easy later switch, while Aston Villa attackers such as Nicolas Jackson and Bournemouth’s Tavernier enter the picture from Gameweek 9. The central aim is to preserve a strong bench, rotate fixtures effectively through at least Gameweek 11 and roll transfers wherever possible.
key_points: Captain Saka against Leeds in Gameweek 6 is a serious option, while Haaland remains essential despite Liverpool away because Ipswich follow in Gameweek 7.
Saka is selected over Palmer because Arsenal’s winger is currently the clearer talisman, leading his side for big chances and shots while underperforming his xG.
Calafiori and Mosquera form the preferred Arsenal defensive double-up, with Calafiori’s attacking role and likely league minutes making him a cornerstone pick.
Verbruggen plus Hull’s Salah is the chosen £4.5m goalkeeper rotation; Raya is passed over to preserve funds and Arsenal slots for Calafiori, Mosquera and Saka.
Monitor Van Hecke after his Netherlands withdrawal, with Vuskovic the likely replacement if injury news rules him out.
Bournemouth’s excellent Gameweek 7-14 schedule supports António Silva now and puts Tavernier on the transfer radar from Gameweek 9.
João Pedro’s knee problem is the key late decision: hold if the absence is short because Groß provides cover, but consider Igor Thiago or an Isak restructure if he is set to miss several weeks.
Gonzalo García is a fixture-led Fulham differential, with Calvert-Lewin identified as a straightforward replacement if he disappoints.

items.title: 55K OVERALL RANK 🌎 | TOM HADLEY'S GAMEWEEK 6 TEAM REVEAL 🎯 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Tom Hadley backs Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier as Gameweek 7 midfield target after early Konsa move
items.summary:
Tom Hadley makes an unusually early Gameweek 6 transfer, selling Luke Shaw for Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa. The move protects 0.2m of value as Konsa rises and Shaw falls, while leaving enough money to upgrade Ibrahim Sangaré to a budget midfielder in Gameweek 7. It is a calculated risk made three weeks before the deadline and across an international break, but Hadley is content to take it because Konsa is a straightforward replacement and the Wildcard remains available if injuries derail the plan.

Hadley is not yet ready to Wildcard despite concerns over Cole Palmer and João Pedro. He likes the core of his squad, particularly his Arsenal defenders, Pascal Groß and Nottingham Forest pair Morgan Gibbs-White and Daniel Muñoz, and prefers to use his bench or occasionally take a hit rather than overhaul a team he largely trusts. Gibbs-White and Muñoz arrive for Matt O’Riley and Solis in Gameweek 5, a hit that fails immediately but is retained for Forest’s appealing away fixtures at Crystal Palace in Gameweek 6 and Ipswich in Gameweek 8.

Captaincy remains open. Palmer holds the armband for now but is only a placeholder amid fitness uncertainty. Hadley considers Gibbs-White a serious differential captain against Crystal Palace, citing his dominant creative involvement, penalties, set pieces and Forest’s stronger away record. Erling Haaland at Liverpool remains the safer default, but Hadley is willing to oppose him given Liverpool’s defensive resilience. Groß is another viable captaincy alternative.

For Gameweek 7, Sangaré is the intended sale because his lack of secure starts undermines his otherwise attractive attacking and DefCon potential. Bournemouth’s Marcus Tavernier is the leading replacement: he has three goals, a huge share of Bournemouth’s attacking involvement, regular shots and possible penalty responsibility if Justin Kluivert is absent. Alex Scott is the steadier alternative at the same price, combining attacking returns with strong DefCon output and set-piece duties. Brentford’s Kevin Schade also appeals if his minutes remain secure, while Aston Villa’s Manzambi, Leeds’ Stack and the 5.0m Yana are longer-term budget options. Hadley aims to preserve his Wildcard until Gameweeks 12-17 if possible, when fixture swings could encourage investment in Liverpool assets such as Alexander Isak and Virgil van Dijk.
key_points: Ezri Konsa replaces Luke Shaw early for Gameweek 6, banking a 0.2m price swing and preserving funds for a midfield move in Gameweek 7.
Morgan Gibbs-White is a live differential captain at Crystal Palace because he is on penalties and set pieces and is heavily involved in Forest’s attacks.
Cole Palmer is the provisional captain but his fitness, along with João Pedro’s, determines whether Hadley needs to rely on his bench or make further moves.
Ibrahim Sangaré is earmarked for sale in Gameweek 7 due to unreliable minutes, despite his attacking threat and DefCon potential.
Marcus Tavernier is the preferred budget-midfield target, with Alex Scott a more durable DefCon-assisted alternative for Bournemouth’s improving fixture run.
Kevin Schade is under consideration as Brentford’s most secure attacking option, although Gameweek 7 brings Liverpool before a better run follows.
The Wildcard is held back unless injuries create a major problem; Gameweeks 12-17 are viewed as potential windows to target fixture swings and Liverpool assets.

items.title: BEST WILDCARD PICKS? 🤔 | THE FPL SCOUTCAST GW6 🚨| FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Haaland, Saka and Palmer anchor a Gameweek 6 Wildcard built for depth
items.summary:
A Gameweek 6 Wildcard is complicated by the unusually long international break, with fitness doubts around Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro still unresolved. The recommendation is not to rush into assumptions on either player, but Palmer remains worth selecting if fit because Chelsea have no European commitments and attractive home matches against Bournemouth in Gameweek 6 and Spurs in Gameweek 8. Joao Pedro is the more difficult call: he is the natural mid-price forward pick, but any absence could leave Wildcard managers needing an immediate transfer. He is retained provisionally because the alternatives lack appeal, although Everton’s Dominic Calvert-Lewin is flagged as a future regret given Leeds’ improving fixture run from around Gameweek 10.

Erling Haaland is viewed as essential despite Liverpool away in Gameweek 6, while Bukayo Saka provides Arsenal attacking coverage and a plausible alternative captain. Arsenal’s fixtures include Leeds at home in Gameweek 6, Everton at home in Gameweek 8 and Hull at home in Gameweek 10, making a double-up on their defence attractive too. Cristhian Mosquera is considered a standout value route into that back line, while Riccardo Calafiori is preferred over Jurrien Timber because he is cheaper and carries fewer immediate minutes concerns. Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres could gain appeal if Kai Havertz’s injury proves serious, particularly if he becomes first-choice and takes penalties, but that role needs confirming.

The final draft favours two £4.5m rotating goalkeepers rather than David Raya, freeing funds for a deeper outfield squad. Guglielmo Vicario and Bart Verbruggen form the suggested pairing, with Brighton trusted more than Fulham over the long term. The defence combines Arsenal security with value and attacking upside: Ezri Konsa, Thomas, Mosquera, Calafiori and Newcastle’s Kieran Trippier. Bournemouth’s Silva and Liverpool’s Jarell Quansah are discussed but discarded to avoid spending too heavily on defenders who may rarely start in a team expected to play the Arsenal pair most weeks.

Pascal Gross is treated as the major midfield lock because of his penalties, set pieces, reliable minutes and price, even allowing for Brighton’s European schedule. Josh King is backed as a £5.5m differential after two goals and promising underlying numbers, while Sharda replaces Morgan Gibbs-White to make the budget work. The completed £100m structure is Verbruggen and Vicario; Konsa, Thomas, Mosquera, Calafiori and Trippier; Gross, Saka, Palmer, Sharda and King; plus Haaland, Gonzalo Garcia and Joao Pedro. Gonzalo Garcia is selected as a short-term third forward for Ipswich and Hull in his next three fixtures, while the overall aim is to retain playable bench depth rather than dead-ending the squad.
key_points: Erling Haaland is an essential Wildcard pick, even with Manchester City visiting Liverpool in Gameweek 6.
Bukayo Saka is Arsenal’s preferred attacking pick and a viable Gameweek 6 captain alternative, while Calafiori and Mosquera offer a strong defensive double-up.
Cole Palmer remains a Wildcard inclusion if fit, with Chelsea’s lack of European football strengthening his appeal.
Joao Pedro is provisionally retained despite his injury doubt, but managers must be prepared to move quickly if he misses Gameweek 6.
Pascal Gross is a midfield priority due to penalties, set pieces, exceptional value and dependable minutes.
Use £4.5m goalkeeper rotation rather than Raya to preserve budget, with Vicario and Verbruggen the preferred pairing.
Gonzalo Garcia is a short-term forward differential for favourable matches against Ipswich and Hull, while Calvert-Lewin is one to monitor for Leeds’ later fixture swing.
Avoid a dead bench on Wildcard: the proposed squad keeps King, Sharda and multiple budget defenders available to cover injuries and rotation.

items.title: THE ULTIMATE CHIP STRATEGY 🍟 | GAMEWEEK 6 ✅ | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Gameweek 13 wildcard plan targets Liverpool return after Arsenal-Man City clash
items.summary:
FPL managers still holding a wildcard are advised to avoid forcing it for Fulham’s short fixture run alone, despite attractive Gameweek 6 matches against Ipswich, Hull and Coventry. Gameweek 6 offers the benefit of reacting to international-break injuries, with Joao Pedro under specialist assessment, while Pascal Gross and selected Fulham assets are obvious targets. But Fulham’s opponents also see those fixtures as winnable, so a transfer or two may be preferable to a full squad overhaul.

Gameweek 7 is a slightly stronger wildcard window for Bournemouth and Tottenham investment. Bournemouth begin a more appealing run and offer options such as goalkeeper Djordje Petrovic, defender Silva, Marcus Tavernier and potentially Ryan; Tottenham assets also become more viable despite their uneven start. The risk is European rotation, particularly around Manchester City’s matches with Liverpool and PSG, while Haaland’s home fixture against Ipswich may be affected by minutes management either side of those games.

The standout later wildcard is Gameweek 13. Managers can save three or four transfers, attack Gameweek 12 by selling Haaland and Arsenal defenders before Arsenal face Manchester City, then wildcard back into a new structure. Liverpool become especially attractive from Gameweek 13, with Sunderland, Chelsea, Leeds, Tottenham and Hull ahead, while Nottingham Forest also improve. The approach also permits a Haaland-and-Alexander Isak forward line or a broader restructure after targeting one-week Gameweek 12 fixtures.

For remaining bench boosts, the recommendation is to use it early rather than struggle to field 15 reliable starters during the congested winter schedule. Gameweeks 8 and 9 suit budget benches: Brentford face Hull in Gameweek 8, Nottingham Forest visit Ipswich, and promoted sides are all at home; Gameweek 9 brings Hull v Ipswich, Coventry v Sunderland, Bournemouth v Leeds and Brentford v Forest. A Gameweek 6 wildcard can also be paired with a Gameweek 7 bench boost, using cheap Fulham and Bournemouth players such as Bernd Leno, Antonee Robinson, Josh King, Petrovic and Tavernier.

Triple-captain options are led by Haaland at home to Hull in Gameweek 16, although managers must monitor the preceding EFL Cup tie and December rotation. Haaland at home to Ipswich in Gameweek 7 has major upside but carries Champions League rotation risk. Bruno Fernandes at home to Coventry in Gameweek 14 is the preferred alternative: his midfield scoring routes and security of starts make him safer than Bukayo Saka against Hull in Gameweek 15. For free hits, Gameweek 12 is ideal for avoiding Arsenal v Manchester City and loading up on Crystal Palace v Hull, Leeds v Coventry, Aston Villa v Ipswich and Brighton v Newcastle; Gameweek 16 offers a second major opportunity to target Manchester City v Hull while avoiding Arsenal v Manchester United and Liverpool v Tottenham.
key_points: Avoid wildcarding solely for Fulham’s Gameweek 6-8 run; Ipswich, Hull and Coventry are not necessarily easy opponents for Fulham.
Gameweek 7 is a strong wildcard entry point for Bournemouth and Tottenham, but European rotation clouds Manchester City selections.
Gameweek 13 is the preferred long-term wildcard window, allowing managers to target Gameweek 12 first and then buy back Haaland, Arsenal assets and Liverpool players.
Use a remaining bench boost by Gameweek 9 where possible, with cheap promoted-team defenders and favourable Brentford, Bournemouth, Forest and Coventry fixtures supporting a playable bench.
A Gameweek 6 wildcard followed by a Gameweek 7 bench boost can exploit Fulham v Hull and Bournemouth v Sunderland with low-cost squad players.
Haaland at home to Hull in Gameweek 16 is the leading triple-captain candidate, provided his EFL Cup and festive minutes look secure.
Bruno Fernandes at home to Coventry in Gameweek 14 is the safer triple-captain alternative because he is less exposed to rotation than Manchester City or Arsenal stars.
Gameweek 12 and Gameweek 16 are the leading free-hit windows, with the former built around avoiding Arsenal v Manchester City and the latter around attacking Manchester City v Hull.

items.title: THE BEST GW6 WILDCARD 🔥 | FPL GENERAL'S WILDCARD TARGETS!  | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Pascal Gross and Erling Haaland anchor Gameweek 6 wildcard plans
items.summary:
A Gameweek 6 wildcard is built around Brighton’s Pascal Gross, Manchester City’s Erling Haaland and Arsenal coverage, with budget left deliberately unspent for later moves to premium options such as Cole Palmer, Bruno Fernandes or Alexander Isak. Gross is the standout value asset after four assists and three goals in five matches, while Haaland remains the leading captaincy option despite an away trip to Liverpool. Bukayo Saka is preferred to Palmer as the premium midfielder because of Arsenal’s form, reliable minutes and stronger underlying output, though Palmer remains a viable alternative if Chelsea’s attack continues to deliver.

The defensive core is Arsenal’s Ezri Konsa and Riccardo Calafiori, plus Brighton wing-back Maxim De Cuyper. Calafiori offers value and attacking upside, while De Cuyper remains difficult to ignore as long as he continues playing out of position on the wing; Pervis Estupinan’s return from injury is a longer-term risk, not an immediate reason to sell. Bournemouth’s Silva is the preferred cheap defender ahead of James Hill because of his early goal threat and regular defensive-contribution potential, with Bournemouth’s schedule improving sharply after Chelsea away. Leif Davis is the leading £4.0m defender thanks to his attacking returns, although Nikola Milenkovic is the upgrade to consider if more money is required in defence.

In midfield, Josh King is a prime Gameweek 6 buy as Fulham begin a run against the three promoted sides and increasingly rely on him as their attacking focal point. Morgan Rogers is hard to omit despite lacking the premium security of Saka or Palmer: he combines strong shot and chance-creation numbers with Chelsea’s high-scoring, low-clean-sheet profile. Marcus Tavernier is another fixture-led option, with Bournemouth facing Sunderland, Manchester United, Leeds, Ipswich and Nottingham Forest after Gameweek 6; Chelsea’s defensive fragility means he is playable immediately, and Lewis Cook’s injury could also improve Tavernier’s penalty prospects.

Joao Pedro stays in the forward line if fit, as his injury flag appears more likely to be managed over the international break than a long-term concern. Nicolas Jackson is the high-upside differential: he looks settled at Aston Villa under Unai Emery and could inherit the consistent No. 9 role that previously made Ollie Watkins such a strong FPL asset, although Villa’s next few fixtures mean he may need benching before their Gameweek 9 run. Goncalo Garcia, Josh King and Dominic Calvert-Lewin are safer cheaper-forward alternatives; Calvert-Lewin in particular is worth holding through Arsenal away rather than repeatedly spending transfers chasing marginal changes among £6.0m forwards.

Goalkeeper preference depends on structure. Lucas Perri Trafford is the set-and-forget £5.0m choice because Leeds look stable and he offers save and bonus potential comparable with David Raya at a lower price, while Raya and a £4.0m reserve provide Arsenal clean-sheet security. An alternative wildcard uses Raya, Calafiori, De Cuyper, Antonee Robinson, Morgan Gibbs-White, Harvey Barnes, Gross, Haaland, Pedro and Garcia, with Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk as a reliable £5.0m bench option for defensive contributions. The central principle is to carry eight playable attackers, accept occasional points on the bench and rotate according to fixtures rather than force transfers every week.
key_points: Captain Haaland in Gameweek 6 away to Liverpool, with Saka and Gross credible alternatives in a week without an obvious runaway captain.
Gross and De Cuyper are priority Brighton picks; retain De Cuyper while he remains deployed high up the pitch despite Estupinan’s gradual return.
Target Josh King for Fulham’s upcoming run against promoted opposition, with Garcia and Calvert-Lewin alternative budget forwards.
Back Arsenal defence through Calafiori and Konsa, while Silva is Bournemouth’s preferred cheap defender ahead of Hill.
Consider Tavernier now or from Gameweek 7 as Bournemouth’s fixture run improves, with Chelsea away not necessarily a fixture to avoid for attackers.
Jackson is an upside Villa differential but may require benching against Newcastle and Manchester City before Villa’s Gameweek 9 fixture swing.
Keep £2.9m-£3.0m in reserve rather than overloading on premiums, preserving routes to Palmer, Fernandes or Isak.
Avoid wasting transfers constantly rotating cheap forwards and defenders; bench Calvert-Lewin or other playable assets for difficult fixtures instead.

items.title: WILDCARDS ACTIVE! 🚨 | FPL CHAI & JOSH'S GW6 WILDCARD DRAFTS! 🔥 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Wildcards target Brighton, Fulham and Spurs rotations ahead of Gameweek 7 bench boost
items.summary:
Gameweek 6 wildcard planning centres on building a strong 15-man squad for a Gameweek 7 Bench Boost, with Brighton, Fulham and Tottenham providing the most attractive short-term fixtures. A draft built around Bernd Leno, Antonee Robinson, Micky van de Ven, Destiny Udogie, Bukayo Saka, Cole Palmer, Pascal Gross, Kevin Schade, Erling Haaland, Gonzalo and Joao Pedro aims to exploit Fulham’s meetings with Ipswich, Hull and Coventry, while Spurs offer Coventry at home in Gameweek 7. The key is having enough bench depth to rotate defenders through tougher fixtures, notably Tottenham away to Manchester United and Chelsea.

Fulham’s triple-up is aggressive but supported by their fixture run and encouraging performance against Manchester United. Leno and Robinson offer clean-sheet and save-point routes, while Gonzalo is preferred as a cheap forward with manager backing and chance potential. There must be an exit plan after the promoted-team run, however, as Bournemouth, Arsenal and Manchester United assets become more appealing from Gameweek 8 onwards. Bournemouth’s run from Gameweek 9 — Leeds, Ipswich, Nottingham Forest, Fulham, Brighton, Hull and Coventry — puts Antoine Semenyo, Marcus Tavernier and defender Antonio Silva firmly on the radar.

Brighton remain close to essential wildcard coverage after scoring freely against Aston Villa, Chelsea and Arsenal. Pascal Gross is seen as a set-and-forget value midfielder, while Kaoru Mitoma, Castulas and centre-back Vuskovic are viable additions for a Gameweek 7 Bench Boost against Crystal Palace. Vuskovic is particularly appealing for DefCon points, set-piece threat and secure minutes. Joao Pedro stays in plans only if fitness is confirmed; any lingering doubt makes him too risky for a Bench Boost squad, although managers should retain a route to buy him back quickly.

Premium decisions remain unsettled. Saka is a stronger captaincy option than Palmer in the immediate period, but Kai Havertz’s injury could reduce Arsenal’s attacking effectiveness and Saka’s appeal. Palmer’s penalty role offers explosive upside, yet Morgan Rogers and the numerous £6m midfielders make the Chelsea midfielder’s premium difficult to justify. Haaland remains viable despite the uncertainty surrounding Manchester City’s 115 charges, though City’s Liverpool fixture limits the appeal of playing a triple-up immediately. Alexander Isak returning early from international duty raises interest in Cody Gakpo as Liverpool’s central forward, but Liverpool’s difficult upcoming schedule means any move is a calculated punt rather than a priority.

Newcastle’s fixtures make Harvey Barnes and Yoane Wissa leading mid-priced options, with Wissa narrowly preferred among the £5.5m-£6.5m forwards because Newcastle should score against Coventry, Crystal Palace, Everton and Fulham. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the more convincing longer-term alternative, particularly if he retains penalties for Leeds. Kevin Schade remains the standout £6m midfielder due to Brentford’s attacking reliability and his secure role, while Tavernier can become an easy sideways move once Bournemouth’s fixture swing arrives.
key_points: A Gameweek 7 Bench Boost encourages two playing goalkeepers and a deep defensive rotation, rather than a standard cheap bench.
Fulham assets are targeted for Ipswich, Hull and Coventry, with Leno, Robinson and Gonzalo the main options but requiring an exit plan afterwards.
Double Tottenham defence is viable for Coventry at home in Gameweek 7, provided it can be benched against Manchester United and Chelsea.
Brighton are strong wildcard targets: Gross is a priority, while Vuskovic offers DefCon, set-piece and clean-sheet upside.
Joao Pedro is selected only with clear fitness confirmation; uncertainty over his status is too risky when Bench Boosting.
Bournemouth become major transfer targets from Gameweek 9, with Tavernier, Semenyo and Antonio Silva benefiting from an outstanding run of fixtures.
Wissa is the preferred cheap forward for Newcastle’s upcoming schedule, while Calvert-Lewin is viewed as the better longer-term alternative.
Schade is the preferred £6m midfielder, with Barnes and Tavernier strong alternatives depending on Newcastle and Bournemouth fixture targeting.

items.title: FPL HIGHER OR LOWER WITH AZ + SAM! ⁉️ | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Josh King emerges as Fulham’s low-owned fixture play as Pascal Groß keeps punishing non-owners
items.summary:
Pascal Groß is the standout early-season value pick despite a modest underlying creative profile, leading FPL scoring on 47 points after three goals and four assists. His returns include a degree of overperformance and some fortunate assists, but at £5.8m he remains a major source of regret for managers who chose cheaper defensive-contribution midfielders such as Brentford’s Yehor Yarmolyuk/Sangaré-type options instead. Groß’s ownership appeal is as much about removing a painful route to rank damage as chasing a sustainable statistical explosion.

Erling Haaland remains worth holding at £15.6m even with only 39 points, fewer than Groß, because he is still the game’s most reliable scorer: five goals broadly match his 4.43 non-penalty xG. The wider premium market does not currently demand major spending, with Bruno Fernandes, Cole Palmer and Bukayo Saka not producing consistently enough to justify sacrificing Haaland. Alexander Isak is attractive as Liverpool’s secure central striker, with four goals from 3.63 non-penalty xG, but £9.1m is difficult to accommodate alongside Haaland and João Pedro; the uncertainty over whether Isak retains penalties after Dominik Szoboszlai takes one is another concern.

The immediate fixture-driven move is toward Fulham. Calvin-Lewin continues to offer excellent value, with 3.12 non-penalty xG close to Isak’s output for far less money, but Leeds’ fixtures worsen. Fulham’s upcoming three matches against promoted teams make Gonzalo and especially Josh King viable replacements or additions. King has only four chances created but posts 14 shots and an exceptional 37 box touches, more than Haaland’s 31, suggesting strong goal potential. At roughly 2.5% ownership, he is a high-upside differential, although there is caution over repeating past mistakes by chasing an appealing budget midfielder too aggressively.

Marcus Tavernier also becomes a strong medium-term target from Gameweek 7, when Bournemouth begin a long favourable run including Sunderland, Manchester United, Leeds, Ipswich, Nottingham Forest and Fulham. He has three goals from 13 shots, two double-digit returns and multiple routes to points. In defence, Arsenal’s best structure is Raya plus Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa rather than the £8.0m Gabriel, who has only five shots and limited additional upside. Newcastle’s Lewis Hall is also appealing: his 25.6 baseline bonus score per 90 gives him a strong chance of bonus even without attacking returns, while Joško Gvardiol’s 37 points and returns in every game come with significant overperformance risk.

Chelsea’s João Pedro remains the preferred attacking asset if fit, while Morgan Rogers is favoured over Cole Palmer on value. Rogers and Palmer have near-identical box involvement, 29 versus 28 touches, but Palmer costs far more and has overperformed his underlying numbers. Saka is a wildcard consideration as Arsenal’s fixtures improve, though uncertainty over penalties when Martin Ødegaard and Viktor Gyökeres are available reduces confidence. Bruno Fernandes is a sell candidate relative to Bryan Mbeumo: Fernandes has created only one big chance, while Mbeumo combines 19 shots, 28 box touches and 10 chances created, and looks unfortunate not to have more than his current returns.
key_points: Hold Haaland despite his price: his five goals closely match his underlying numbers and his captaincy reliability outweighs the appeal of inconsistent premium midfielders.
Josh King is a leading Gameweek transfer target, with 37 box touches and three favourable fixtures against promoted sides making him a low-owned Fulham differential.
Consider Calvin-Lewin to Gonzalo if moving early onto Fulham’s fixture swing, but Calvin-Lewin’s 3.12 non-penalty xG means selling him carries form risk.
Target Marcus Tavernier from Gameweek 7 as Bournemouth enter a long favourable run; he already has three goals, 13 shots and two double-digit hauls.
Choose Raya, Calafiori and Konsa over Gabriel in an Arsenal defensive triple-up, as Gabriel’s £8.0m price lacks sufficient attacking upside.
Morgan Rogers is preferred to Cole Palmer on value, while João Pedro remains Chelsea’s best FPL attacker provided his injury is minor.
Lewis Hall’s elite baseline bonus score makes him an appealing Newcastle defender, while Gvardiol’s perfect return streak looks vulnerable to regression.
Bruno Fernandes remains underwhelming for his price, with only one big chance created; Mbeumo offers stronger all-round involvement for substantially less money.

items.title: GUESS THE PLAYER! 🤔 | The Scout Quiz FPL GW6
items.headline: Riccardo Calafiori emerges as the Gameweek 6 Leeds differential
items.summary:
Riccardo Calafiori is identified as the defender to target for Gameweek 6 after scoring only one point in Gameweek 5 despite averaging 5.8 points per match across the season so far. The Arsenal defender’s strong underlying points record keeps him on the radar despite the latest blank.

Calafiori faces Leeds in Gameweek 6, making him a potential defensive and attacking differential for managers seeking a London-based defender with a favourable fixture. The recommendation rests on backing his season-long output rather than reacting to a single low-scoring gameweek.
key_points: Riccardo Calafiori scores one point in Gameweek 5.
The Arsenal defender averages 5.8 FPL points per match this season.
Calafiori plays Leeds in Gameweek 6.
His Gameweek 5 blank should be weighed against his stronger season-long scoring rate.

items.title: Palmer Captain?! 🧢 | Tom Freeman's GW6 Bus Team
items.headline: Palmer edges Haaland for captaincy as four-transfer rebuild looms
items.summary:
The current squad is likely to be rolled this week, with the aim of building to four free transfers before a planned restructure around Gameweek 7 or 8. The team was assembled with a Bench Boost in mind, so retaining flexibility now is viewed as more valuable than making a short-term move.

A multi-transfer overhaul is expected because the original Bench Boost-focused structure may no longer be the best fit. Banking transfers would allow three or four coordinated changes rather than piecemeal fixes, reducing the risk of taking hits or being trapped by the current squad shape.

Captaincy is close. Cole Palmer is the preferred option, particularly because Chelsea are at home, although Erling Haaland remains a viable high-upside alternative despite facing Liverpool away. Haaland is considered captainable in any fixture, but the away match makes the decision less straightforward.

Bruno Fernandes also enters the discussion for Manchester United at home to Tottenham, especially for managers who own him. However, United's lack of consistent attacking form tempers confidence, making Palmer the steadier captaincy choice among the options discussed.
key_points: Roll the transfer to move closer to four free transfers ahead of a likely Gameweek 7 or 8 squad rebuild.
The planned overhaul reflects a squad originally constructed for Bench Boost, with several moves likely needed to reshape it.
Cole Palmer is the leading captaincy choice due to Chelsea's home fixture.
Erling Haaland remains a legitimate captain option even away to Liverpool, but the fixture is difficult.
Bruno Fernandes is a possible captain against Tottenham at home, though Manchester United's form is a concern.

items.title: WILDCARDS ACTIVE! 🔥 | FPL EARLY THOUGHTS GW6 💭 |  FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Bruno Fernandes survives the wildcard cull as managers weigh Gameweek 7 Bench Boosts
items.summary:
The central wildcard divide is whether managers have already used Bench Boost. Tom, who has played it, can dead-end a goalkeeper slot and field only two forwards, freeing funds for a balanced XI featuring Erling Haaland, João Pedro, Bruno Fernandes, Pascal Groß, Morgan Gibbs-White, Kevin Schade and Harvey Barnes. Managers still holding Bench Boost need a playable third striker and stronger bench, making a targeted Gameweek 7 wildcard-and-chip strategy more attractive but more restrictive financially.

Tom’s draft backs Kinsky in goal, double Arsenal defence through Calafiori and Kiwior, Everton’s James Tarkowski, Fulham newcomer Aen Gruber and Leeds defender Mahmovic. Arsenal remain a leading clean-sheet target despite a poor result against Brighton, although their Champions League, Carabao Cup and Premier League schedule raises rotation concerns for all but the safest assets. Tarkowski is preferred to cheaper Everton colleague Branthwaite because of his superior durability, attacking threat and reliable defensive-contribution potential, while Mahmovic is viewed as a possible season-long hold despite tougher immediate fixtures.

The most contrarian premium call is retaining Bruno Fernandes at £11.9m. He has only one return in five gameweeks, but his chance creation, box involvement and expected goal involvement remain strong, and he is a dependable 90-minute captaincy option in Gameweeks 6, 8 and 10. Bukayo Saka and Cole Palmer offer alternative premium routes, but Saka’s minutes could be managed during Arsenal’s congested schedule. Schade is favoured among Brentford attackers for his minutes and underlying numbers, Barnes benefits from Newcastle’s lack of European football, and Gibbs-White remains Forest’s talisman and likely penalty taker, though his £8m value is questioned.

The preferred structure is 3-5-2 or 4-5-1, with Haaland and a fit João Pedro as the two forwards. The panel argues that forwards offer too few routes to points compared with midfielders and defenders, particularly because they lack defensive-contribution returns; even well-performing options such as Dominic Calvert-Lewin are not matching the value elsewhere. For the Gameweek 7 Bench Boost draft, Saka is joined by Groß, Morgan Rogers, Schade and Manchester City’s Enzo, with Haaland, João Pedro and Fulham striker Gonzalo up front. Gonzalo is selected for penalties and Fulham’s favourable run against Ipswich, Hull and Coventry, while Enzo is a differential based on set pieces, advanced potential and expected strong minutes under Enzo Maresca.

Gameweek 7 planning centres on Manchester City’s home match against Ipswich, Tottenham’s Coventry fixture and Fulham’s favourable schedule. The unresolved question is how aggressively to chase the Bench Boost: loading up on short-term City and Fulham assets could create a major one-week gain, but may force later transfers and weaken the longer-term squad. Josko Gvardiol is under scrutiny despite consistent early returns because City’s defence has looked vulnerable and their fixtures worsen after Ipswich; cheaper defenders such as Fulham’s Aen Gruber or Bournemouth’s Antonio Silva may offer better value through defensive contributions. For Gameweek 6 captaincy, Tom favours Haaland against Liverpool, while the Bench Boost draft has Saka at home to Leeds, with Bruno also a viable alternative against Tottenham.
key_points: Tom’s post-Bench-Boost wildcard structure uses two forwards only, with Haaland and João Pedro preferred over a third striker because midfielders and defenders are delivering better value.
Bruno Fernandes remains a wildcard option at £11.9m due to elite underlying numbers, secure 90-minute potential and captaincy relevance despite four blanks in five gameweeks.
Double Arsenal defence is attractive for projected clean sheets, but Calafiori and Kiwior carry rotation risk during a run containing three Champions League weeks and a Carabao Cup tie.
Tarkowski is the preferred Everton defender over Branthwaite because he combines defensive-contribution points, set-piece threat and a safer injury record.
Schade, Barnes and Gibbs-White are mid-priced midfield candidates, with Schade’s underlying data, Barnes’s lack of European rotation and Gibbs-White’s penalties all boosting their appeal.
Managers retaining Bench Boost are urged to consider activating a Gameweek 7 wildcard, targeting City v Ipswich, Spurs v Coventry and Fulham’s run of Ipswich, Hull and Coventry.
Enzo is proposed as a low-cost Manchester City midfield differential because of set pieces, Maresca’s trust and a potential advanced role, though City’s European schedule remains a minutes risk.
Haaland is Tom’s preferred Gameweek 6 captain against Liverpool, while Saka is the alternative captain in the Bench Boost-focused draft for Arsenal’s home match with Leeds.

items.title: GROSS CAPTAIN?! 🫡 | FPL General's GW6 Bus Team
items.headline: Groß enters captaincy contention alongside Saka and Havertz
items.summary:
Pascal Groß is a serious captaincy option after an outstanding season, with his current fixture considered good enough to keep the armband on him for now. His form makes him difficult to overlook even against alternatives with stronger home fixtures.

The final decision depends partly on players returning safely from the international break. Any fitness issues, fatigue or unexpected absences could alter the captaincy picture, so the armband is not treated as locked in.

Bukayo Saka at home to Leeds is the leading alternative, with Arsenal’s favourable home fixture offering a potentially safer high-upside route. Kai Havertz, also at home to Bournemouth, is another viable Arsenal captaincy candidate, particularly if he remains central to the attack. Groß remains firmly in the debate, but the choice is likely to come down to balancing his season-long output against the appeal of Arsenal’s fixtures.
key_points: Pascal Groß currently holds the captaincy armband because of his excellent season and a reasonable fixture.
Bukayo Saka at home to Leeds is a major alternative captaincy option.
Kai Havertz faces Bournemouth at home and is also under consideration for the armband.
International-break fitness and availability news could decide the final captaincy call.
The central trade-off is Groß’s sustained form versus Arsenal’s attractive home fixtures.

items.title: WILDCARDS ACTIVE! 🚨 |THE FPL WATCHLIST GW6 🔎 | WISSA, SAKA, PALMER 🎯 | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Bukayo Saka challenges Cole Palmer as the premium Wildcard midfielder for Gameweek 6
items.summary:
Wildcard planning centres on whether to invest in Arsenal's attack or lean fully into their defence. Arsenal remain viewed as the league's best defensive side despite the 3-0 defeat to Brighton, making Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Ezri Konsa an attractive triple-up. Konsa's £4.6m price makes him especially appealing, although William Saliba's eventual return creates a medium-term minutes risk; Calafiori also carries some rotation potential. The alternative is Bukayo Saka, whose underlying numbers make a powerful case: he leads midfielders for big chances, ranks near the top for shots on target and expected goal involvement, takes penalties and appears to be Arsenal's primary goal threat. Saka also gives managers a credible captaincy alternative to Erling Haaland, notably when Arsenal host Leeds in Gameweek 6.

Cole Palmer is less convincing as a premium pick at present. Chelsea's goals are spread between Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro, while Joao Pedro is the side's clearest scoring threat and Palmer's output is not matching Saka's all-round data. Rogers, at £7.7m, is considered outstanding value because he is nailed, creates heavily and offers strong expected involvement, while Joao Pedro remains a priority if fitness news is positive after the international break. His injury status is the key uncertainty: if he is ruled out for multiple weeks, managers can move on, but if fit he is both a strong value selection and a potential captain against Bournemouth.

In the mid-priced bracket, Morgan Gibbs-White is favoured as a long-term set-and-forget option, particularly with Nottingham Forest facing three away matches in four and showing stronger form on the road. Pascal Gross remains a reliable, nailed budget asset and penalty taker, while Semenyo is a higher-risk differential due to potential Champions League rotation. Harvey Barnes is attractive after Newcastle's attacking injuries and departures, with Coventry, Aston Villa, Crystal Palace, Everton and Fulham ahead, but his minutes remain less secure than his per-90 output suggests. Brentford's Schär is preferred to Tavernier for immediate upside, although Bournemouth's fixture swing from Gameweek 9 makes Tavernier and Antonio Silva viable future targets.

Up front, Gonzalo Garcia is the standout Wildcard forward around £6m because Fulham face all three promoted clubs in succession before Aston Villa and Newcastle. His slow start is excused by difficult early fixtures, and Rodrigo Muniz remaining on the bench supports his role. Yoane Wissa is less appealing despite Newcastle's favourable run, having missed a penalty, produced limited recent shot volume and increasingly operated deeper. Brighton's Castillo and Newcastle's Barnes are also considered stronger alternatives, while Dominic Calvert-Lewin is identified as a likely later move ahead of a favourable home run from Gameweek 10. Haaland remains the default captain, especially away to Liverpool, although Saka and a fit Joao Pedro offer viable alternatives.
key_points: Bukayo Saka is the leading premium midfield target on Wildcard, with elite big-chance, shot-on-target and expected-involvement numbers plus penalty duties.
Arsenal's defensive triple-up of Raya, Calafiori and Konsa is viable, but Konsa and Calafiori face some future rotation risk when William Saliba returns.
Cole Palmer is not essential while Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers provide cheaper Chelsea coverage, though Palmer remains a high-upside Bournemouth captaincy punt.
Joao Pedro's fitness update is crucial: if cleared, he becomes a major value pick and captaincy contender; if ruled out for weeks, managers can sell comfortably.
Morgan Gibbs-White and Pascal Gross are favoured stable midfield options, while Semenyo and Harvey Barnes offer higher-risk differentials.
Gonzalo Garcia is preferred to Yoane Wissa among £6m forwards because Fulham play the three promoted sides in their next three matches.
Dominic Calvert-Lewin is a planned future target ahead of Gameweek 10 home fixtures against Spurs, Coventry, Ipswich and Fulham.
Erling Haaland is the current default captain for Liverpool away, with Saka at home to Leeds the main alternative.

items.title: My early transfer thoughts for Gameweek 6 #fpl #fantasypremierleague #fpltips
items.headline: Joao Pedro fitness decides whether Palmer becomes Fernandes for Gameweek 6
items.summary:
The Arsenal defensive triple-up remains the foundation of the squad despite conceding three against Brighton. David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Konces are all viewed as strong holds because Arsenal are still expected to deliver clean sheets over the coming weeks. Lewis Hall also keeps his place after demonstrating his attacking potential against Hull, with Coventry the next opportunity for further returns.

Cole Palmer is expected to be fit for Bournemouth at home despite his yellow flag, but there is temptation to turn him into Bruno Fernandes for captaincy. That move is only realistic if Joao Pedro is sold, making Pedro’s injury update the key factor before Gameweek 6. Morgan Rogers is an easy hold after his first blank of the season against Brentford, while Erling Haaland and Yoane Wissa are retained; Wissa has disappointed, but Coventry away is not the fixture to sell him before. Szoboszlai has underperformed but is likely to get one more week because there are more urgent decisions elsewhere.

If Joao Pedro is ruled out, Gonzalo Garcia is a potential replacement, with Ipswich away, Hull at home and Coventry away across the next three gameweeks. Selling Pedro for Garcia creates the funds to make Palmer-to-Fernandes happen, with a plan to buy Pedro back later. The preferred outcome, however, is to keep Pedro if possible: he remains a strong longer-term option and could simply be benched for De Cuyper in a 4-4-2. Another route is selling Sangare for Sharda, Tavernier or Barnes, allowing both Joao Pedro and De Cuyper to be benched. If Raya or Calafiori suffer an international-break injury, downgrading one to a cheaper defender would free funds for Szoboszlai to Bukayo Saka, with £1.1m already in the bank.
key_points: Keep Raya, Calafiori and Konces despite Brighton conceding three, with Arsenal clean sheets still expected soon.
Hold Palmer for Bournemouth at home if fit, but Bruno Fernandes is the preferred captaincy-driven alternative.
Joao Pedro’s fitness determines whether a Pedro-to-Gonzalo Garcia transfer can fund Palmer to Fernandes.
Gonzalo Garcia has a favourable three-game run of Ipswich away, Hull at home and Coventry away.
Haaland, Wissa and Morgan Rogers are holds, with Wissa given at least Coventry away before any sale.
Szoboszlai is likely to receive one more week unless an Arsenal defensive injury creates a route to Saka.
If Joao Pedro is unavailable, benching him for De Cuyper and playing 4-4-2 is preferable to selling him unless funds are needed.
A Sangare move to Sharda, Tavernier or Barnes is an alternative midfield solution that permits benching both Joao Pedro and De Cuyper.

items.title: MY FPL GW6 WILDCARD DRAFT! 📝 #fpl #premierleague #wildcard
items.headline: Calafiori, Raya and Timber anchor an aggressive triple-Arsenal defence for Gameweek 6
items.summary:
The provisional Gameweek 6 Wildcard is built around Arsenal’s defence, with David Raya in goal alongside Riccardo Calafiori and Jurrien Timber. A £4.0m reserve goalkeeper completes the goalkeeper group. The approach prioritises Arsenal’s clean-sheet potential while using Jan Paul van Hecke and Leeds defender Muharovic as two active lower-cost defensive options, rather than relying on non-playing budget picks from Ipswich or Coventry. That should provide enough cover to avoid spending transfers on defenders over the next few months.

Cole Palmer remains in midfield, although there is a live consideration to downgrade him to Morgan Rogers and release substantial funds elsewhere. Morgan Gibbs-White keeps his place, while Pascal Groß and Kevin Schade make up the rest of the first-choice midfield after Schade’s strong start to the season. Marcus Tavernier is held on the bench as a longer-term Bournemouth fixture play, giving the squad a usable fifth midfielder rather than a dead spot.

Erling Haaland is the non-negotiable premium forward. João Pedro is currently included, but his Gameweek 6 place depends on a fitness update, making him the key uncertainty in the front line. Yoane Wissa is the third striker and offers another regular attacking option, although the draft remains flexible if Pedro is unavailable.

The Wildcard is not yet activated. Early transfers are being used to catch possible price rises before a likely activation ahead of Gameweek 6, but the squad retains a Free Hit as a fallback if those moves do not work out. The central trade-off is committing heavily to Arsenal’s defence and retaining Haaland and Palmer, versus downgrading Palmer to Rogers to make the overall structure easier to fund.
key_points: The current Wildcard draft uses a triple-Arsenal defensive core of David Raya, Riccardo Calafiori and Jurrien Timber.
Jan Paul van Hecke and Leeds defender Muharovic are selected as playing budget defenders, reducing the need for defensive transfers.
Cole Palmer stays for now, but a move from Palmer to Morgan Rogers is under consideration to free up funds.
Morgan Gibbs-White, Pascal Groß, Kevin Schade and bench option Marcus Tavernier complete the midfield structure.
Erling Haaland is locked in, while João Pedro needs a positive fitness update to remain in the Gameweek 6 squad.
Yoane Wissa is the third forward in the provisional draft.
The Wildcard remains unactivated while early transfers target price changes, with the Free Hit available if the plan goes wrong.

items.title: BEST ATTACK & DEFENCE 🎯 | FPL EXPERT'S GW6 TRANSFER PLANS  ✅ | FPL Tips 26/27
items.headline: Palmer remains Tom Freeman’s Gameweek 6 captain despite fitness flag as transfers are banked
items.summary:
Tom Freeman’s Bench Boost delivers 63 points and a green arrow to around 120,000 overall, with all 15 players featuring. The chip is helped by returns from Lewis Hall (13), Erling Haaland’s captaincy (12), Barry (6), Verbruggen (6), Stach (5) and Muhamovic (6), although Wissa misses a penalty and blanks after replacing the injured Joao Pedro. Freeman chooses Wissa over Igor Thiago and Liam Delap partly for his longer-term fixture run, but acknowledges that the alternatives would have scored better in Gameweek 5.

For Gameweek 6, Freeman is set up to roll a transfer for a fourth free move in Gameweek 7. He has £2.1m in the bank and expects his Bench Boost-built squad to need a wider restructure soon, potentially involving the return of Joao Pedro. Palmer is his provisional captain at home to Bournemouth, with the Chelsea midfielder’s flag considered more likely to be load management than a serious injury. However, any lingering pre-deadline uncertainty could push Freeman towards vice-captain Haaland away at Liverpool; Haaland has nine attacking returns in 11 meetings with Liverpool, including goals in each of his last two.

The principal selection issue is Dominik Szoboszlai at home to Manchester City. Freeman sees the Liverpool midfielder as a growing problem after limited recent output, while Joe recommends either benching him for Neco Williams away at Crystal Palace or selling him for Brighton’s Pascal Gross. Freeman leans towards holding, as Williams has a playable fixture and preserving transfers offers flexibility. Gross is nevertheless viewed as an outstanding long-term pick due to penalties, set pieces and Brighton’s prolific attack, with Sunderland away and Crystal Palace at home next.

Brighton lead the league for both goals and expected goals after five gameweeks, while Manchester City, Brentford and Manchester United also rate strongly in attack. Chelsea’s 10 goals significantly exceed their expected-goals total, adding caution to triple-up investment, whereas Fulham and Nottingham Forest appear more promising than their goal tallies suggest. Defensively, Arsenal remain the standout and double coverage is recommended, particularly with Leeds visiting in Gameweek 6. Nottingham Forest’s underlying defensive numbers also support holding their assets, while Liverpool’s defence rates well statistically but faces an awkward run including Manchester City, Brentford and Arsenal.
key_points: Palmer is the current Gameweek 6 captain at home to Bournemouth, but Haaland away at Liverpool is the leading alternative if Chelsea fitness news remains unclear.
Freeman plans to roll his transfer and enter Gameweek 7 with four free transfers, anticipating a later squad restructure after using Bench Boost.
Szoboszlai is the main weak link; starting Neco Williams instead or moving Szoboszlai to Pascal Gross are viable alternatives to rolling.
Gross is a strong midfield target because he is on penalties and set pieces for the league’s most productive attack, Brighton.
Joao Pedro is a likely future buy-back, with Freeman preferring a Chelsea attacking double rather than a triple-up over the longer term.
Double Arsenal defence remains the clearest defensive strategy for Gameweek 6, with Arsenal’s underlying numbers still the best in the league.
Nottingham Forest’s strong expected-goals-conceded figures support holding their defenders despite only one clean sheet so far.
Chelsea’s attacking output is running ahead of expected goals, while their defence has conceded more than underlying numbers suggest, so both trends carry regression risk.
